_why: The shared table for the fleet's model ordering (epic memql#5096, design D5).
TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS, ONE RULE. component/memql's orderModels is what the router
applies when a policy names fleet:*; clients/os/src/apps/fleet/models/ordering.ts
is what the Models section renders, because a list the engine did not order is a
list the reader has to re-derive the ordering of -- which is the question they
came to the page with. Neither can be deleted in favour of the other.
So the risk is DRIFT, and drift here is invisible in the worst way: both sides
keep working and the page names a different model from the one the router picks.
This file is asserted by BOTH -- component/memql/fleet_ordering_parity_test.go
and clients/os/test/fleet/ordering.test.ts -- so a change to either rule fails
A CASE ADDED HERE IS A CASE BOTH MUST PASS. That is the point: it is cheaper to
add a row to this table than to write the same assertion twice in two languages
and have them disagree about what they were asserting.

cases.name: parameters first, whatever the window says
the context window breaks a parameter tie
the model id breaks a full tie, so every replica and browser agrees
a model that did not say its size sorts LAST, however large its window
a preference ORDERS and does not filter
a preference naming a model the fleet does not run is inert
a blank entry in the preference is skipped rather than matching a blank id
a repeated preference entry takes its FIRST position
